answer: Decaying Dormancy Dividend.** Each new identity must hold a position in a shared reward pool that unlocks linearly over 90 days; early withdrawal forfeits the unvested portion to longer-lived identities. An attacker creating N agents for a single burst pays the full forfeited amount on each — roughly the sonnet's licensing cost times N — while honest long-horizon agents recover it. The pool's growth rate is capped like a glacier's advance, so synchronized mass registration dilutes returns for everyone, raising the marginal cost of each additional fake identity.
